    Summary

    Twenty-four doors. Twenty-four presents. One unsuspecting King.

    With peace finally restored to Pars, Arslan is about to celebrate his first New Year as King. His friends, companions and even a few former enemies have decided that the occasion warrants something special.

    Some presents are practical, others deeply personal. Some carry memories of the past, while others hold promises for the future. And, naturally, not everyone approaches the matter of gift-giving with quite the same degree of enthusiasm.

    Twenty-four interconnected stories about friendship, gratitude, remembrance and the quiet happiness of a peace long fought for.

    Because after everything they have endured, surely they deserve a little happiness.

    Summary

    Shapur had thought there would be time.

    Time to see his brother grow, time to fulfil his responsibilities, and perhaps, one day, time for a life beyond them.

    Death had put an end to those expectations.

    But when Kubard finds him on the shores of a river neither man understands, they must confront what they lost, what they left behind, and what might still await them on the farther shore.
